title: Man who allegedly stabbed Toronto police officer has died: SIU
article: The man who allegedly attacked and stabbed Toronto Police officer Constable Jeff Blair has died, according to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU).
38-year old Peter Lumanglas was reportedly shot during an altercation with Constable Blair after a routine traffic stop.
The incident happened Sunday evening near Bathurst Ave. and Wilson Rd. during a routine traffic stop conducted by Constable Blair.
Lumanglas was in the car at the time and when he was pulled over, an altercation ensued whereby the officer was stabbed.
Constable Blair then fired off several gun shots that hit Lumanglas.
The injured officer and Lumanglas were then rushed to Sunnybrook hospital.

Lumanglas remained in critical condition in hospital, later succumbing to his injuries. Krystle Magallanes, the girlfriend of Lumanglas told Global News on Friday that both his legs had been amputated - if he had survived - he would have been in a wheelchair.

Magallanes said that she was told by Sunnybrook Hospital at approximately 10a.m. on Friday that Lumanglas was in stable condition. He died at 10:30a.m., though she was not told until approximately 4 hours later at 2p.m..
Magallanes told Global News earlier in the week that she didn't think Peter was capable of attacking a police officer.
"They're saying Peter was shot and stuff, and when they said he stabbed a cop, I said no way," Magellanes said. "Of all my time knowing Peter, there's no way, he's not that violent."
Lumanglas was a father of a five month old baby and had recently finished an eighth month sentence for drug trafficking last New Year's eve.
